sana: hey folks :wave: I'm a new hire trying to get local services running. docker-compose up brings up redis but Postgres keeps dying. I get Permission denied when the container tries to write to /var/lib/postgresql/data, and after I fiddled I also hit `FATAL: password authentication failed for user \"postgres\"` when I try to psql. here's my compose snippet:

```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    volumes:
      - ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
```

I'm on macOS (Docker Desktop). Any quick checklist for new hires?

alex: welcome! :wave: two quick things — host-mounted PGDATA often has wrong ownership because the container's postgres user has uid 999. Try:

```
sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata
```

or easier, use a named volume instead of a host bind:

```yaml
volumes:
  pgdata:
services:
  db:
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```

Also if you already initialized the dir with a different image or user, Postgres will keep the old auth files.

mike: +1. If you switched images or recreated without clearing the data dir, you'll get password issues. Do:

```
docker-compose down -v
rm -rf ./pgdata/*   # careful, only for local dev
docker-compose up
```

alex: mac note — Docker Desktop uses gRPC-FUSE for mounts which can cause weird perms and slowness. For reliable dev either use a named volume or bind to a tmp path and chown. Example to check uid inside container:

```
docker run --rm postgres:15 id postgres
```

sana: thanks! running `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata` now. one more newbie question: how do I discover the right uid if image changes?

mike: run the id command alex posted or `docker run --rm postgres:15 sh -c 'getent passwd postgres'`. You can also inspect ownership on host with an alpine helper:

```
docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/host alpine sh -c 'stat -c "%u:%g" /host/pgdata'
```

infra-bot: onboarding-checklist updated — Added note about using named volumes for Postgres on mac, and a short troubleshooting section. https://redwood-internal/onboarding/db-setup :white_check_mark:

sana: that fixed it :tada: chown to 999 and `docker-compose down -v` cleared the stale init state. Postgres came up and psql connects. One last thing: any recommended Redis setup for local dev?

alex: nice! for Redis just use `image: redis:7` and skip volumes unless you want persistence. super simple: `ports: - "6379:6379"`. If you want an example compose with both services, ping me and I’ll drop one in the onboarding repo.

sana: will do, thanks all :pray:
